gaps.sentence: If only I ___ my umbrella — I am getting soaked!
gaps.hint: present regret about an earlier decision
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus the past perfect expresses a present regret about a past decision: had brought.

gaps.sentence: I'll lend you the tent ___ you bring it back dried.
gaps.explanation: 'Provided (that)' introduces the condition under which something will happen.

gaps.sentence: If only I had taken that job — I ___ much happier now.
gaps.hint: mixed wish: past event, present result
gaps.explanation: 'Now' anchors the result in the present, so 'would be' is needed.

gaps.sentence: He would be healthier if he ___ so much red meat.
gaps.hint: an unreal present habit, past simple
gaps.explanation: For an unreal present habit, the if-clause uses the past simple: did not eat.

gaps.sentence: Unless something urgent ___, I will be at my desk all morning.
gaps.hint: unless introduces the exception, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the exception to the plan and takes the present simple: comes up.

gaps.sentence: We will refund the item provided that you ___ the receipt.
gaps.hint: provided that plus a present requirement
gaps.explanation: 'Provided that' states a requirement using the present simple: have.

gaps.sentence: He wouldn't be so tired today ___ so late last night.
gaps.explanation: Past condition with present result: if + past perfect, would + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: We'll be fine ___ the forecast is wrong.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless the forecast is wrong' = if it is not wrong.
